root_cause.text: A race condition between the heartbeat worker and intel_engine_park_heartbeat() due to non-atomic reads and writes of the `engine->heartbeat.systole` pointer, allowing both paths to obtain the same reference and call `i915_request_put()` twice, causing a refcount underflow.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "The heartbeat worker reads engine->heartbeat.systole and calls i915_request_put() on it when the request is complete, but clears the pointer in a separate, non-atomic step. Concurrently, ... intel_engine_park_heartbeat() reads the stale non-NULL systole pointer and calls i915_request_put() on it again, causing a refcount underflow." The fix replaces the non-atomic read+clear with `xchg()` to atomically exchange the pointer with NULL, ensuring only one caller obtains the non-NULL pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix race condition in heartbeat systole handling by using atomic xchg.
intent_record.what: Replaced non-atomic read-and-clear of engine->heartbeat.systole with an atomic xchg operation, and added a conditional restore if the request is not yet completed.
intent_record.how: Ensures thread-safe access to the heartbeat systole pointer by atomically exchanging it with NULL, then either dropping the completed request or restoring the pointer if still in flight.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a NULL guard before releasing the heartbeat request reference.
intent_record.what: Replaced `fetch_and_zero(&engine->heartbeat.systole)` with explicit `xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL)` and added a NULL check before `i915_request_put(rq)`.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that `i915_request_put` is only called when the retrieved pointer is non-NULL, avoiding a potential NULL pointer dereference or unnecessary function call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor heartbeat parking to use xchg and explicit NULL check for clarity, preserving existing behavior.
intent_record.what: Replaced direct call to i915_request_put(fetch_and_zero(...)) with explicit xchg to NULL, storing result in local variable, then conditionally calling i915_request_put if non-NULL.
intent_record.how: The runtime behavior is unchanged because i915_request_put(NULL) is a no-op; the conditional check is purely cosmetic.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the race condition in heartbeat systole handling by using atomic xchg, which is the exact root cause described.

The group adds a NULL guard before releasing the heartbeat request reference, which directly addresses the race condition that causes a double put and refcount underflow. This change is intended to prevent one of the racing paths from performing the decrement when the pointer is already NULL, mitigating the root cause.
The refactoring introduces xchg for atomic access to the systole pointer, directly addressing the non-atomic reads and writes that caused the race condition.

candidates.rationale: Non-atomic read of the systole pointer introduces a race window; between this read and the later NULL write, another thread (intel_engine_park_heartbeat) may obtain the same reference and put it, leading to double put and refcount underflow.
This put can be executed at the same time as a put in intel_engine_park_heartbeat() because both paths read the same reference without atomic synchronization, causing a refcount underflow.

Non-atomic write to the systole pointer can overwrite a value that was already atomically exchanged by another thread, preventing proper NULL assignment and allowing the other thread to already have released the reference.
